back: The willingness and ability to take risks and organise land, labour and capital to run a business.
A person who identifies an opportunity, takes risks and organises resources to produce goods or services.
Showing initiative: spotting opportunities and acting on them with energy and creativity.

front: Rewards of the factors of production
back: Land: rent. Labour: wages. Capital: interest. Enterprise: profit.
Risk-taking, innovation, determination, self-confidence, leadership, communication, decision-making, planning.
Independence, profit, personal satisfaction, flexibility, recognition.
Risk of losing savings, irregular income, long hours and stress, no paid leave or pension.

front: Importance of enterprise to the economy
back: Jobs, output, innovation, competition, tax revenue, exports, use of local resources.
Skills (planning, record keeping) can be learned; qualities (determination, self-confidence) are personal characteristics.
